Watches `@agent` markers in your vault, dispatches forked subagents, and stores results in LanceDB with vector + FTS + graph. Multi-agent \"Drop & Forget\" workflow.\n\n> Looking for the legacy ledger-first extension (predecessor project)?\n> See [kylebrodeur/pi-qmd-ledger](https://github.com/kylebrodeur/pi-qmd-ledger).\n> This project was renamed twice: `pi-qmd-ledger` → `pi-knowledge-store` (intermediate) → `pi-vault-mind` (current).\n\n## Features\n\n- **Passive File Watcher** — drop `@agent:<role>` (or `@agent-<role>`) markers in any Obsidian note. Save. The watcher detects the marker, groups by role, and dispatches isolated subagent forks. The original request block is preserved in the note; only the running-status line is updated with the result summary. `@agent:main` is reserved for the current interactive session and is never auto-dispatched — sweep it manually with `/vm main sweep`. No chat pollution, no manual triggers.\n- **Multi-Agent Architecture** — five specialist agents under the `vault-mind-{role}` skill naming: **Manager** (interactive orchestrator), **Miner** (research + entity extraction), **Broadcaster** (NotebookLM artifacts), **Heavy-Lifter** (external delegation), **Watcher** (passive file observer).\n- **LanceDB Vector + FTS + Graph** — hybrid semantic + keyword search with automatic entity extraction and BFS graph traversal. All local, no external binaries.\n- **JSONL Source-of-Truth + LanceDB Index** — every fact lives in a durable, human-readable, version-control-friendly `collections/*.jsonl` file. The LanceDB index is derived and rebuildable via `/vm reindex --all --reembed`.\n- **Bidirectional Obsidian Sync** — substantial entries (`>200 chars` or tagged `decision`/`insight`/`requirement`) auto-write to `Vault/Agent/Inbox/`. Graph entities render as Obsidian Canvas files.\n- **Vault-Scoped Configuration Surface** — Vault Mind setup/config now lives under `<vault>/.vault-mind/`, with the Obsidian setup wizard and `/vm setup` both writing the vault-local surface instead of a shared global config.\n- **Interactive Setup Wizard** — the Obsidian setup wizard handles first-run runtime/install/provider/folder/preferences/review flow, and `/vm setup` remains available for CLI/repair use.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  User prompt                             │\n│  e.g. \"draft login\"                      │\n└──────┬──────────────────────────────────┘\n       │\n       ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Injector regex match                    │\n│  → matches \"draft\\s+(\\S+)\"              │\n└──────┬──────────────────────────────────┘\n       │\n       ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  query collections/main.jsonl            │\n│  where tag=\"login\" + inject artifact.md  │\n└──────┬──────────────────────────────────┘\n       │\n       ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  Appended to system prompt               │\n│  → LLM now has pre-fetched context       │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n\nData Layer:\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  JSONL WAL (collections/*.jsonl)        │\n│  ─ durable, human-readable, versionable │\n│       │                                  │\n│       ▼ (auto-embed on append)           │\n│  LanceDB (.lancedb/)                    │\n│  ─ vector search + FTS + graph          │\n│       │                                  │\n│       ▼ (graph extraction)               │\n│  Graph Tables (entities + relations)     │\n│  ─ entity linking + traversal            │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nSee [`docs/architecture/index.md`](docs/architecture/index.md) for the full agent flow.\n\n## Obsidian Counterparts & Requirements\n\npi-vault-mind works on any directory, but for the **full Obsidian experience**, you need a few things in Obsidian itself:\n\n### Required: An Obsidian vault\nJust point `/vm setup` at any directory used as an Obsidian vault. pi-vault-mind auto-detects `.obsidian/` and respects `.obsidian/`, `.git/`, `.trash/`.\n\n### Recommended: Official Obsidian CLI (1.12+)\n\nThe [official Obsidian CLI](https://help.obsidian.md/cli) lets you install plugins, themes, and manage vault state from the terminal. **This is the safest, most direct install path** for pi-vault-mind's required plugins.\n\nInstall: Open Obsidian → **Settings → General → Command line interface** → enable. Follow the prompt to register the CLI to your system PATH. Restart your terminal. Test: `obsidian help`.\n\nThen run:\n```bash\nobsidian plugin:install id=obsidian-git enable\nobsidian plugin:install id=obsidian-breadcrumbs enable\nobsidian plugin:install id=graph-analysis enable\nobsidian plugin:install id=actions-uri enable\nobsidian plugin:install id=obsidian42-brat enable\nobsidian plugin:install id=obsidian-pi-vault-mind enable\n\nFull walkthrough: see [`docs/integrations/OBSIDIAN_SETUP.md`](docs/integrations/OBSIDIAN_SETUP.md).\n\n### Recommended: Obsidian Community Plugins\n\n| Plugin | Install ID | Why | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| **obsidian-git** | `obsidian-git` | Auto-commits vault changes for backup & conflict resolution. Heavy-Lifter uses git worktrees for isolated refactors. | Essential |\n| **Breadcrumbs** | `obsidian-breadcrumbs` | Parses typed edges (`agent:related-to`, `agent:derived-from`) in YAML frontmatter. The recommended way to display the agent-extracted knowledge graph in Obsidian's UI. | Highly recommended |\n| **Graph Analysis** | `graph-analysis` | Co-citation discovery, Jaccard similarity on the native Obsidian graph. Surfaces \"always cited together but not yet linked\" notes — a key agent discovery signal. | Highly recommended |\n| **Actions URI** | `actions-uri` | `x-callback-url` endpoints so the Manager agent can trigger Obsidian UI commands (open notes, run commands) from pi. | Recommended |\n| **Vault Mind plugin** | `obsidian-pi-vault-mind` | Native setup/status/chat UI and HTTP bridge integration. | Recommended |\n\n### Recommended: `notesmd-cli` (headless alternative)\n\nFor headless operations, CI, or when Obsidian isn't running, use [Yakitrak/notesmd-cli](https://github.com/Yakitrak/notesmd-cli). It does everything the official CLI does but doesn't require Obsidian to be open.\n\n```bash\nbrew tap yakitrak/yakitrak && brew install yakitrak/yakitrak/notesmd-cli\n# or scoop, AUR, etc.\n\nnotesmd-cli add-vault /path/to/vault\nnotesmd-cli create \"Note.md\" --content \"...\" --append\n```\n\nUse the official `obsidian` CLI when Obsidian is running; use `notesmd-cli` when it isn't.\n\n### Beta plugins via BRAT\n\nFor beta plugins not in the official store:\n\n```bash\n# Install BRAT first\nobsidian plugin:install id=obsidian42-brat enable\n\n# Then add beta plugin URLs via BRAT's interface, or:\n# In Obsidian: Settings → BRAT → Beta Plugin List → Add\n```\n\n### Curated vault-local skills\n\n`pvm setup` installs the supported Obsidian and NotebookLM skills into the\nvault-local Pi agent directory:\n\n```bash\npvm setup /path/to/your/vault\n```\n\nThe skills live under\n`<vault>/.vault-mind/.pi/agent/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. `pvm run` disables\nPi's implicit global/project skill discovery and explicitly loads only these\ncurated skills plus skills provided by packages installed in the same\nvault-local agent directory. Do not install these skills globally for a Vault\nMind session; global copies defeat vault isolation and can create skill-name\nconflicts.\n\n- `obsidian-markdown` — Obsidian-flavored Markdown syntax\n- `obsidian-bases` — valid `.base` database views\n- `json-canvas` — Canvas JSON used by graph sync\n- `obsidian-cli` — Obsidian CLI operation\n- `nlm-skill` — NotebookLM CLI and MCP workflows\n\nThese skills let the **Miner, Broadcaster, and Heavy-Lifter agents** produce\nvalid Obsidian content without changing the identity of the interactive main\nagent.\n\n### Built-in Obsidian features used\n\n| Feature | How pi-vault-mind uses it |\n|---|---|\n| **YAML frontmatter properties** | Strict schema for typed edges (`agent:related-to`, `status: needs-podcast`, `domain:`, `tag:`) |\n| **Callouts** | `> [!info]`, `> [!warning]` for syntheses and contradictions |\n| **Embeds** | `![[Note]]` to transclude summaries into synthesis docs |\n| **Obsidian Bases (`.base`)** | Agent-generated dynamic tables/boards/kanbans in `Agent/Tasks/` |\n| **JSON Canvas (`.canvas`)** | `vm_sync(format=\"canvas\")` writes entity graph as Canvas JSON |\n| **Obsidian Sync** | Primary sync mechanism across devices |\n\n### Optional: NotebookLM integration (Broadcaster)\n\nThe Broadcaster agent can generate podcasts, study guides, and slide decks from vault content via the [notebooklm-mcp-cli](https://github.com/jacob-bd/notebooklm-mcp-cli) MCP server. Requires Google account login.\n\n---\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### Prerequisites\n\n- **Node.js** 24.19.0+ (matches `engines` in `package.json`)\n- **Embedding Provider** — choose one:\n  - `@xenova/transformers` — built-in, no external deps (uses all-MiniLM-L6-v2, offline-capable)\n  - `ollama` — requires Ollama running locally with `embeddinggemma` (higher quality)\n  - `modal` — optional, **bring-your-own deploy**: offload embedding + bulk re-index to a cloud GPU service and sync vectors down for offline search (see [docs/integrations/MODAL_EMBEDDING.md](docs/integrations/MODAL_EMBEDDING.md)). Default behavior is unchanged until you opt in.\n\n> **On the Modal provider:** the local providers above work for everyone with\n> zero infrastructure — that's the default. `modal` is an **optional, self-hosted\n> tier**: you deploy your own copy of the service (`uvx modal deploy modal/app.py`\n> from a clone of this repo) to your own Modal account and point the extension at\n> *your* URL + token. There is no shared/hosted endpoint — a deployment's URL and\n> bearer token are private to whoever owns it. (A standalone PyPI package for the\n> server may come later.)\n\n### 1. Install and set up the vault-local runtime\n\nInstall the first-class `pvm` CLI once, then run setup against a vault:\n\n```bash\nnpm install --global pi-vault-mind\npvm setup /path/to/your/vault\npvm run /path/to/your/vault\n```\n\n`pvm setup` is safe to repeat. It installs or updates the required Vault Mind,\ncontext, model-routing, task, and subagent extensions inside\n`<vault>/.vault-mind/.pi/agent/`; installs the curated `obsidian-cli`,\n`obsidian-markdown`, `obsidian-bases`, and `json-canvas` skills; and\nmerge-safely scaffolds Vault Mind, model-router, and main-agent configuration.\nOn first run it also creates stock `.pi/agent/system.md` and vault-root\n`AGENTS.md` baseline regions. All of these are preserved on repeat runs —\nexisting user configuration, collections, model choices, and personalizations\nare never overwritten.\n\nRefresh only extensions, tools, and skills without touching vault\nconfiguration:\n\n```bash\npvm setup --resources-only /path/to/your/vault\n```\n\nAudit the isolated runtime without changing it, or repair it in place:\n\n```bash\npvm check-deps /path/to/your/vault\npvm check-deps --fix /path/to/your/vault\n```\n\nAdd `--strict` to fail when optional tools are missing and `--obsidian` to\ninclude recommended Obsidian plugin checks.\n\nRun either mode without a global installation:\n\n```bash\nnpx --yes pi-vault-mind setup /path/to/your/vault\nnpx --yes pi-vault-mind run /path/to/your/vault\n```\n\nInstalling only the Pi extension remains supported:\n\n```bash\npi install npm:pi-vault-mind\npi -e npm:pi-vault-mind\n```\n\n### 2. Configure interactively when needed\n\nInside Pi, use the wizard to choose or change embedding providers, folder\nlayout, and other user-facing settings:\n\n```text\n/vm setup\n```\nFor a non-interactive repair inside Pi:\n\n```text\n/vm setup --vault /home/you/Obsidian/MyVault --remoteUrl https://your-embedding-service-url.example.com --model embeddinggemma\n```\n\nConfig is written to the vault-local Vault Mind surface under\n`<vault>/.vault-mind/` rather than a shared global config file.\n\nYou can re-run `/vm setup` anytime to view or change settings, and the\nObsidian plugin's setup wizard uses the same extension-owned routes.\n\n### 3. Start using\n\n```\nvm_append(collection=\"main\", mode=\"autopilot\", entry={\"id\":\"1\",\"domain\":\"auth\",\"fact\":\"JWT tokens expire after 1 hour\",\"tag\":\"security\"})\nvm_search(collection=\"main\", query=\"token expiry\")\n```\n\nEntries are automatically embedded and stored in LanceDB. If graph is enabled, entities and relations are also extracted.\n\n### 4. Adapt the config\n\nEdit `<vault>/.vault-mind/vault-mind.config.json` to match your domain:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"version\": 2,\n  \"collections\": {\n    \"main\": {\n      \"path\": \"collections/main.jsonl\",\n      \"schema\": [\"id\", \"domain\", \"source\", \"fact\", \"tag\", \"artifact\"],\n      \"dedupField\": \"fact\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"injectors\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"draft-context\",\n      \"regex\": \"draft\\\\s+(\\\\S+)\",\n      \"collection\": \"main\",\n      \"filterField\": \"tag\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"vaultMind\": {\n    \"dataDir\": \".lancedb\",\n    \"embedding\": {\n      \"remoteUrl\": \"http://127.0.0.1:11434\",\n      \"model\": \"embeddinggemma\",\n      \"dim\": 768\n    },\n    \"ftsEnabled\": true,\n    \"graph\": { \"enabled\": true, \"canvasSync\": false }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n## Using Vault Mind agent identities\n\nVault Mind keeps the interactive Pi session on the unrestricted `main` persona\nunless you explicitly select a specialist boundary. Bundled specialist skills\nare available resources; merely loading them does not change the active\npersona.\n\n### Start the vault-local main agent\n\nFrom the vault directory, start Pi in the current terminal:\n\n```bash\npvm run\n```\n\nYou can launch a different vault from anywhere or use the package without a\nglobal install:\n\n```bash\npvm run /path/to/your/vault\nnpx --yes pi-vault-mind run /path/to/your/vault\n```\n\n`pvm run` defaults to the current terminal. This is the recommended Obsidian\nTerminal profile command. Use a vault-path placeholder supplied by the plugin,\nor provide the vault's absolute path. Override the launch mode when needed:\n\n```bash\npvm run --same-terminal /path/to/your/vault\npvm run --new-window /path/to/your/vault\npvm run --auto /path/to/your/vault\n```\n\n`--new-window` opens a dedicated Terminal/iTerm window. `--auto` uses the\ncurrent terminal when attached to a TTY and falls back to a new window\notherwise. The packaged shell launcher remains available for direct use as\n`scripts/vault-pi.sh`.\n\nIn every mode, the launcher runs Pi inside the target vault with its\nconfiguration isolated under `<vault>/.vault-mind/.pi/agent/`. It also prevents\ntwo launcher-managed Pi processes from running for the same vault and removes\nthe PID file when an inline session exits.\n\nCheck the active persona after startup:\n\n```text\n/vm identity status\n```\n\nA normal main-agent session reports:\n\n```text\nPersona: main\nEffective boundary: none (main agent)\n```\n\n`Injection` may report `enabled` or `disabled`. An enabled injector still\napplies no boundary while the persona is `main`.\n\n### Use specialist agents without changing the main session\n\nNormally, leave the interactive session on `main` and dispatch specialist work\nthrough the passive watcher. Both marker forms are equivalent:\n\n```text\n@agent:miner\nResearch and extract the durable facts from this note.\n```\n\nor\n\n```text\n@agent-miner\nResearch and extract the durable facts from this note.\n```\n\nThe watcher runs that work as an isolated specialist job, preserving the\nrequest block in the source note and replacing only the running-status line\nwith a result summary. It does not turn the interactive terminal into the\nMiner persona. The same applies to `@agent:broadcaster`, `@agent:manager`,\nand `@agent:heavy-lifter`.\n\n`@agent:main` is reserved for the current interactive session and is never\nauto-dispatched. To sweep reserved markers into the active session:\n\n```text\n/vm main sweep\n/vm main sweep path/to/note.md\n```\n\n### Explicitly change the interactive persona\n\nUse an identity boundary only when the current interactive session itself\nshould follow a specialist capability contract:\n\n```text\n/vm identity set miner\n/vm identity set broadcaster\n/vm identity set manager\n/vm identity set heavy-lifter\n```\n\n| Persona | Intended interactive boundary |\n|---|---|\n| `main` | Unrestricted primary agent with the full configured toolset |\n| `manager` | Orchestrates collections, publishing, and subagents; does not run Bash |\n| `miner` | Extracts and stores knowledge; does not run Bash or publish |\n| `broadcaster` | Produces presentation artifacts; does not run Bash or write durable knowledge |\n| `heavy-lifter` | Performs file and Bash work in isolation; does not write durable knowledge or publish |\n\n`/vm identity set <role>` persists the selected persona, enables boundary\ninjection, and applies on the next agent turn.\n\nUse the remaining controls to inspect or suspend that selection:\n\n```text\n/vm identity status\n/vm identity off\n/vm identity on\n```\n\n- `off` disables boundary injection without discarding the selected persona.\n- `on` re-enables the configured persona boundary on the next agent turn.\n- `status` shows the configured persona, injection switch, effective boundary,\n  and any environment overrides.\n\nRestore the safe main-agent default with:\n\n```text\n/vm identity set main\n/vm identity off\n/vm identity status\n```\n\nThe final status should show `Effective boundary: none (main agent)`.\n\n### Configuration and environment overrides\n\nIdentity controls are stored in the vault-local configuration:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"vaultMind\": {\n    \"identities\": {\n      \"activeRole\": \"main\",\n      \"injectBoundaries\": false\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\nThe canonical path is\n`<vault>/.vault-mind/vault-mind.config.json` under\n`vaultMind.identities`. Identity commands preserve any existing\n`vaultMind.identities.roles` allowlists.\n\nLaunch automation and explicit specialist forks can override the saved values\nfor one process:\n\n```bash\nVAULT_MIND_AGENT_ROLE=miner VAULT_MIND_IDENTITY_INJECTION=on pi\nVAULT_MIND_IDENTITY_INJECTION=off pi\n```\n\n`VAULT_MIND_AGENT_ROLE` takes precedence over `activeRole`.\n`VAULT_MIND_IDENTITY_INJECTION=off` suppresses every boundary, while `on`\nenables the explicitly selected role. Missing, `main`, `none`, and unknown\nroles all resolve safely to the unrestricted main agent.\n\n### Troubleshoot an unexpected specialist boundary\n\n1. Run `/vm identity status` and check both the configured persona and any\n   reported environment overrides.\n2. If an environment override is present, exit Pi, unset\n   `VAULT_MIND_AGENT_ROLE` and `VAULT_MIND_IDENTITY_INJECTION`, then relaunch.\n3. Run `/vm identity set main`, followed by `/vm identity off`.\n4. Send the next agent turn and re-run `/vm identity status`; boundary changes\n   take effect on the next turn.\n5. Confirm Pi was started for the intended vault and uses\n   `<vault>/.vault-mind/.pi/agent/` as `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`.\n\nDo not edit `SYSTEM.md` or an agent skill to change the interactive identity.\nThose files provide operating instructions and resources; persona selection\nbelongs in `vaultMind.identities` or an explicit environment override.\n\n## Example domains\n\n### Research
